issues.description: The problem specification and UML refer to an interface named 'Milkable', but the solution repository defines and uses an interface named 'Dairy' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java) while leaving src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java empty. Several classes (Goat, Seal) implement 'Dairy' but the example Main and the problem text use 'Milkable'. This naming mismatch (Milkable vs Dairy) creates confusion mapping the specification to the implementation and can lead to compilation/type errors if code expecting 'Milkable' is used together with classes implementing 'Dairy'.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across all artifacts. Replace the 'Dairy' interface with the expected 'Milkable' interface (or vice versa) consistently: (1) rename src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java to src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java (or update its declaration to 'public interface Milkable'), (2) have Goat and Seal implement Milkable, (3) remove the empty Milkable.java stub, and (4) ensure all references (including commented examples in Main and the problem statement wording) use the same identifier 'Milkable'. This restores a single, consistent identifier for the milkability concept and avoids type/name mismatches.
